html:
The Potawatomi are an Algonquian people of the western Great Lakes, from lower Michigan around the south end of Lake Michigan into Illinois, Indiana and Wisconsin. They call themselves Neshnabé, a form of Anishinaabe.

With the Ojibwe and Odawa they form the Council of Three Fires, in which they are the youngest brother and the "keepers of the fire". They farmed, fished and hunted, and were close trading partners and allies of New France, fighting beside the French into the 1760s.

The site of Chicago lay in their land, and they fought at the Battle of Fort Dearborn there in 1812. Under the Indian Removal Act most were forced west in the 1830s; the Potawatomi Trail of Death of 1838 from Indiana killed dozens. Groups ended up in Kansas and Oklahoma, while others stayed around the Great Lakes and in Canada.
